newsitem.title: FRANCE: Haiti's Aristide gets UNESCO human rights prize.
newsitem.headline: Haiti's Aristide gets UNESCO human rights prize.

text.p: Haiti's former priest-president Jean-Bertrand Aristide on Wednesday received UNESCO's prize for human rights education for his work in favour of human rights and democracy in his Caribbean country.
Aristide told the award ceremony he received the prize on behalf of "all those fighting for world peace and justice".
He said he would spend the $10,000 prize on Radio Timoun, a radio station run by children and broadcasting for them.

Federico Mayor, director-general of the United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organisation, said concern for participation, sharing and dialogue had been Aristide's motto through his career.
Aristide, elected in 1990, was ousted in a coup in 1991 and returned to power three years later following a U.S. military intervention.
Elected President Rene Preval took over from Aristide in 1996 in Haiti's first democratic handover.
